phase: Manage Frames Inline + Frame Background Image Rotation
milestone: Manage Frames now renders in the same screen as Working View/Runtime Preview instead of a full-screen modal, and a Frame's background image can now be rotated -- and rotation renders identically in Builder's own preview and root Studio's Reader-facing render
slice: Two fixes shipped together, from the user's own verbatim report: "i think the manage frame opens up as seperate window and we are not able to see how it is affecting the frame, so we will need to open manage frames as part of same screen. also when i choose image option spin/rotate is missing." Fix A: Manage Frames previously rendered inside the full-screen #wb-modal overlay (currentNav='frames' was a member of the MODAL_NAVS Set), obscuring Working View/Runtime Preview behind a dark scrim -- so a Theme Author editing a Frame's fields had no way to see the live effect on the actual Scene. Fixed by removing 'frames' from MODAL_NAVS; WORKING_VIEW_PASSTHROUGH_NAVS already correctly kept 'frames' rendering a live specimen and needed no change -- Frame fields now mount inside the persistent #wb-context-panel column, beside the still-visible, still-updating Working View canvas, exactly like every other in-place-editable screen. Fix B: a Frame Variation's Background field already offered an 'image' option (from the Image-Typed Frame Variations sprint) but had no rotation control at all -- fixed by adding frameImageRotation (default 0, via _ensureFrameFieldDefaults's established reconciliation discipline) plus a real 0-359 degree Rotation slider, wired through the exact translate-to-rect-centre/rotate/translate-back convention already proven for Image/Graphics/Text Experience content rotation. The rotation transform was added in lockstep to BOTH rendering engines -- tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js's _paintHolder (rotating the uploaded background image around the mat rect's own centre, inside its existing clip region) and root Studio's renderer/slideRenderer.js's _drawPictureFrameFill (rotating around the frame-fill rect's own centre) -- satisfying Creator Governing Rule #5 (Publish Fidelity): whatever a Theme Author sees in Builder's own preview is exactly what Studio's Reader-facing renderer paints. Confirmed via direct code read that _resolveArtworkFields's wholesale Object.assign(merged, variation.fields) already carries any additive fields.* key straight through to art/border._artwork with zero extra wiring, and that builder.js's _externalizeFrameVariationImages compile step needed no changes since it only ever rewrites fields.frameImage specifically, leaving every other fields key (including the new frameImageRotation) to ride through unfiltered. Verified via a decisive 16-assertion Playwright suite rendering a real, two-colour test image (pure magenta on the left half, pure cyan on the right half) through both engines at rotation=0 and rotation=180, sampling the correct visible 'ring' pixel in each engine's own distinct inset convention (Builder's scaled matInset+matPx/2 formula; Studio's simpler literal-pixel matWidth-as-inset convention) -- confirming rotation=0 shows magenta on the left in both engines and rotation=180 shows the swap to cyan on the left in both, byte-for-byte identical between Builder's preview and Studio's real render. One real test-authoring bug was found and corrected during verification, not an app bug: the first sample point (25% of the outer holder rect's width) landed inside the content-rect's own separate, LATER opaque fill call, which occludes the mat band's own image beneath it by design (the established concentric wall-border-mat-content band-fill technique) -- corrected to sample within the genuinely visible ring between matInset and contentInset instead. Full regression across feature1_frameimage_verify.js (18/18), Feature 2 Phase A/B/C suites (14/8/10, Place-hosted Experience rendering), the Place Guardrails runtime suite (10/10), and both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2, 30/30 each) all pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js, tools/world-builder-v2/js/projectModel.js, tools/world-builder-v2/js/services/engineRuntime.js, and renderer/slideRenderer.js.
